cards.q: What is queuing in QoS and what is the modern answer?
cards.a: Queuing decides the order packets leave an interface when it is congested. The modern answer is CBWFQ (class-based weighted fair queuing) with LLQ (low latency queuing) for delay-sensitive voice.

cards.q: List the queuing mechanisms and the need each one maps to.
cards.a: FIFO (first in first out, no QoS), WFQ (per-flow fair, default legacy), PQ (strict priority, critical only), CBWFQ (per-class weights, modern default), and LLQ (priority plus CBWFQ, for voice).

cards.q: What is CBWFQ and what does each class receive?
cards.a: CBWFQ is class-based weighted fair queuing where each class (matched by class-map) gets a guaranteed bandwidth share using the bandwidth command, services packets by proportional weight, and uses per-queue tail drop.

cards.q: What is LLQ and what risk does its priority class carry?
cards.a: LLQ is a strict priority queue added to CBWFQ (priority queue + CBWFQ). Its priority class is served first but is rate-limited (policed) with pq bandwidth, because an unconstrained priority class can starve other traffic.

cards.q: How do the commands 'priority', 'bandwidth', 'queue-limit', and 'fair-queue' differ in queuing config?
cards.a: priority defines a strict priority class (LLQ), bandwidth gives a guaranteed share, queue-limit sets per-class queue depth, and fair-queue enables per-flow queuing inside a class.

cards.q: Why can PQ starve lower queues and how does LLQ avoid that?
cards.a: PQ is strict so it can starve lower queues; LLQ polices its priority class so it cannot consume all the bandwidth.

cards.q: Where does queuing occur and under what condition does it matter?
cards.a: Queuing is applied egress and only matters under congestion.

cards.q: Voice traffic is experiencing jitter; what is the likely cause and fix?
cards.a: No LLQ/priority class is configured for voice. Place voice in a priority (LLQ) class so it is served first.

cards.q: Other classes are being starved on an interface with a priority queue; what is the likely cause?
cards.a: The priority class is too large (over-provisioned). Reduce the priority bandwidth limit so lower queues still get service.

cards.q: A queue is filling and causing drops; what command-level setting controls it?
cards.a: queue-limit controls per-class queue depth to manage tail drop.

cards.q: What is the difference between PQ and WFQ in selection and priority?
cards.a: PQ selects by strict priority and risks starvation; WFQ selects per-flow and provides fairness.

cards.q: What command shows queuing statistics on an interface?
cards.a: show policy-map interface (or show policy-map interface Gi0/1) and show queueing interface.
